newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares post gains for third day.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares post gains for third day.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in active trading on Thursday for the third consecutive day with the Maof index reaching an all-time high, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.84 percent, or 2.25 points, to 269.00 on a heavy all-share turnover of 158 million shekels against 130 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.06 percent higher at 277.76. Its previous high was reached on February 18 when the Maof reached 277.73.

"The market looks very good and it continues to rise on increased activity. It is clear that the trend is positive and expectations for a rate cut of 0.3 percentage point on Monday support the trend," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.
The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.
"Such a rate cut is only symbolic but in the long term the central bank will continue to lower the rates," Scharia added.

Gidi Halperin, investments manager at Meitav Securities and Investments, said the market was also reacting to positive first-quarter earnings reports and rising volume. "This is a very strong market and it will continue to rise until the end of the year," he said.

Halperin added that the recovery of the primary market was also adding to investor confidence. "If nothing dramatic happens on the political front and on Wall Street the stock market will rise sharply in the short term."
Traders noted that the market might be affected next week by increased activity on the part of options speculators ahead of the expiry date of the May Maof options contract on Thurday.

Mofet Israel Technology Fund gained 0.75 percent to 188 agorot. Mofet said it is planning to raise $26 million for its public traded venture capital fund and another $70 milion for a new private venture capital fund.
Traders noted that most of the activity was concentrated in bank shares ahead of the public offering of Bank Leumi shares and warrants on May 27 in an effort to speed up bank privatisation.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which gained 1.25 percent to 366 agorot on volume of 10 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.75 percent to 711 agorot on turnover of 9.3 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which surged 4.25 percent to 554 agorot.
